title: views-shell.json
description: The views-shell user configuration. The Chrome extension keeps it as a single chrome.storage.sync item under the key "config", so it is sized for the chrome.storage.sync quotas: 102,400 bytes total (QUOTA_BYTES), 8,192 bytes per item (QUOTA_BYTES_PER_ITEM) and 512 items (MAX_ITEMS). A valid configuration serialises to at most 8,192 bytes; tools/validate.py enforces that on every example. Presence in "plugins" means enabled; built-ins appear only as deviations (docs/architecture.md, settings store).

schemaVersion.description: Configuration format version. The JSON number 1; the string "1" is rejected.

theme.description: The active theme. views-shell reads Omarchy theme directories; Chrome follows the same theme through the BrowserThemeColor policy (docs/architecture.md section 4).

name.description: Theme directory name, for example "noir" or "all-black".

chromeThemeId.description: Chrome Web Store theme id Chrome should wear for consistency, for example the All Black theme mkplpffahhkjfocfbfapcemhhkgmljpn.

plugins.description: Enabled plugins as ids, each with its per-plugin settings object. The key is the plugin id; the value is validated against that plugin's contributes.configuration schema, so an empty object means "enabled, all defaults". Absence means disabled; built-ins appear only as deviations.

bar.description: Bar layout: geometry and the ordered surface entries of its three sections.

height.description: Bar height in DIP; also its exclusive zone.

keybindings.description: User overrides of plugin-declared bindings, compositor-neutral (schemas/keybinding-rendering.md). The user wins: an entry here replaces the binding a plugin declared for the same command.

commandRef.description: A command id (local) or plugin-id/command (qualified). Overrides normally use the qualified form.

key.description: Compositor-neutral key chord: modifiers then one key, joined by +. Mod is the user's $mod. Example: Mod+Shift+Escape.

barEntries.description: Ordered bar section entries, each naming a plugin's bar-widget surface as plugin-id/surface-id.
